main_text.p: ominus tamen elephanticorum calorem neutiquam augere poteft: imò corruptionem & putredinem potius intenderet, eò quòd ftatim extra fua vafa corrumpitur. Diu enim integer confiftere nequit, fuo calore & fpiritu, à quibus conferuatur orbatus. Deinde nullam detergendi ac refrigerandi vim ipfum habere fatis perfpicuum Cap.11.est. Galenus item libro ad Glauconem fe-cundo. Oribafius feptimo Synopfeos, & de Cap.51.Morborum curatione tertio. Aetius Ser-mone primo tetr. quarto. Ægineta quarto Cap.63.de Re medica, iis qui cum elephantiasi conflictantur, mirabile esse auxilium viperarum esum affirmant. At vero ipsorum animalium penuria, uti nobis licebit Andromachi theriaca. Galenus libro de theriaca ad Pisonem huius auxilij usu se elephanticis succurisse ait. Aetius loco supra dicta hanc antidotum elephantiasin saepe curare recensèt. Ægineta fales theriacos idem praestare narrat. Quomodo autem parentur, docet nos Galenus eodem ad Pisonem libro, & Aetius loco iam citato. The "Cap.123." note stands beside "mone primo" and "Cap.1." beside "de Re medica"; they are placed in the text where they stand, so the note placement above is approximate for the lower ones, which are written as printed in the margin. The "Cap.123." and "Cap.1." notes are not yet placed in the paragraph above and should be read as margin notes beside the lines "Ser-mone primo" and "de Re medica". Doubtful readings: "fales" (Ægineta fales theriacos) [?]; "locofupra" printed without a space; "docetnos" shown with a space in the scan. The word "recensèt" is copied with an accent as shown on the scan and may be a printing variant; "fe-cundo" and "Ser-mone" are hyphenated line-end words with printed hyphens.
